name: Backpack
description:
A sturdy canvas pack with leather shoulder straps, a drawstring throat and a buckled weather flap. Reinforced seams keep a traveller's daily gear together without the bulk of a rigid frame.

Holds up to 30 lb of contents within 1 cubic foot. The flap sheds light rain but the pack is not waterproof. Sold empty; equipment lashed outside it still adds its full weight.

weight.notes: Adjusted empty weight for a canvas pack with leather fittings; excludes all contents and externally lashed gear.

source.title: Devil's Table: Goods & Provisions
source.reference: General Store / Containers: original description and project price, empty weight and capacity; 2014 rules baseline.
source.license: Original project content; distribution license pending.

name: Pouch
description:
A soft leather pouch with a drawstring closure and a loop for a belt. It keeps coins, small tools and other loose belongings close to hand.

Holds up to 6 lb of contents within one-fifth of a cubic foot. The opening admits small objects rather than long or bulky equipment. Sold empty; it is neither waterproof nor a substitute for a spell component pouch.

weight.notes: Adjusted empty weight for a small unlined leather belt pouch, including cord and belt loop.

source.title: Devil's Table: Goods & Provisions

name: Sack
description:
A coarse woven sack with a doubled seam and a short cord for tying its mouth. It folds flat when empty and is commonly used for grain, provisions or bundles of loose goods.

Holds up to 30 lb of contents within 1 cubic foot. It has no shoulder straps, lining or rigid protection, and its weave will not retain liquids. Sold empty.

weight.notes: Adjusted empty weight for a coarse cloth sack and tie cord; no lining or fittings.

source.title: Devil's Table: Goods & Provisions

name: Chest
description:
A substantial wooden chest with iron hinges, carrying handles and a hasp that accepts a separate lock. The close-fitting lid keeps stored clothing and supplies covered during ordinary travel.

Holds up to 300 lb of contents within 12 cubic feet. This is bulky household or wagon storage, not a wearable pack. Sold empty and without a lock; it is not watertight.

weight.notes: Adjusted empty weight for a light boarded chest with iron fittings; excludes a separate lock and contents.

source.title: Devil's Table: Goods & Provisions
source.reference: General Store / Containers: original description and project price, empty weight and capacity; 2014 rules baseline.

name: Lockbox
description:
An iron-bound wooden box fitted with a small keyed lock. A felt-lined base keeps coins, seals and other valuables from rattling against the wood. One matching key is included in the listed price and weight.

Holds up to 10 lb of contents within 0.15 cubic feet. The lock discourages casual access, but the box can be carried away and is neither fireproof nor waterproof. Sold empty; it is usually ordered for a customer rather than kept on a village shelf.

weight.notes: Adjusted empty weight includes the wooden case, iron bands, fitted lock, felt lining and one key.

source.title: Devil's Table: Goods & Provisions
source.reference: General Store / Containers: original description and project price, empty weight and capacity; ordinary keyed lock adjudicated under the campaign's 2014 rules.

name: Barrel
description:
A coopered wooden barrel held by iron hoops and supplied with a fitted head and bung. It is intended for bulk storage of water, ale or suitable dry provisions.

Holds up to 40 US gallons, subject to a 334 lb contents limit. This is cart or storeroom equipment; a filled barrel is far heavier than its empty weight suggests. Sold empty, without a tap. Keep the staves maintained before relying on it for liquids.

weight.notes: Adjusted empty weight for a light coopered barrel, hoops, head and bung; all liquid or dry contents are additional.

source.title: Devil's Table: Goods & Provisions
source.reference: General Store / Containers: original description and project price, empty weight and capacity; 2014 rules baseline. Liquid measure is the US gallon.
source.license: Original project content; distribution license pending.

name: Crate
description:
A reusable slatted wooden crate with handholds and a loose wooden lid. It gives bundled merchandise more support than a sack while remaining light enough for ordinary deliveries.

Holds up to 80 lb of contents within 4 cubic feet. Gaps between the boards admit rain and dust; small or delicate goods need wrapping. Sold empty with its lid; rope, nails and packing material are separate purchases.

weight.notes: Adjusted empty weight for slatted light wood with a loose lid; excludes lashings and protective packing.

source.title: Devil's Table: Goods & Provisions
source.reference: General Store / Containers: original description and project price, empty weight and capacity; 2014 rules baseline.
source.license: Original project content; distribution license pending.

name: Basket
description:
An open wicker basket with a woven handle and a broad, stable base. It is useful for market purchases, gathered produce and supplies that benefit from ventilation.

Holds up to 40 lb of contents within 2 cubic feet. The open top gives no protection from rain or spilling, and the weave cannot hold liquids or fine powders without a separate liner. Sold empty.

weight.notes: Adjusted empty weight for a wicker basket and handle; excludes any liner, lid or contents.

source.title: Devil's Table: Goods & Provisions
source.reference: General Store / Containers: original description and project price, empty weight and capacity; 2014 rules baseline.
source.license: Original project content; distribution license pending.

name: Bottle
description:
A clear glass bottle with a narrow neck and a fitted cork. Its contents can be inspected without opening it, making it useful for drinks, oils and other compatible liquids.

Holds up to 1 US quart with a 2 lb contents limit. The glass is breakable and the bottle has no protective carrying case. Sold empty with its cork; it is an ordinary vessel, not a prepared potion.

weight.notes: Adjusted empty weight for thin glass and cork; no liquid, padding or carrying case is included.

source.title: Devil's Table: Goods & Provisions
source.reference: General Store / Containers: original description and project price, empty weight and capacity; 2014 rules baseline. Liquid measure is the US quart.
source.license: Original project content; distribution license pending.

name: Flask
description:
A small glazed earthenware flask with a narrow mouth and a cork stopper. It slips into a pouch or pack and keeps a modest portion of drink or oil contained.

Holds up to 1 US pint with a 1 lb contents limit. The fired clay can crack if dropped; this is a storage vessel, not a fireproof bottle. Sold empty with its stopper.

weight.notes: Adjusted empty weight for a small thin-walled earthenware flask and cork; excludes its contents.

source.title: Devil's Table: Goods & Provisions
source.reference: General Store / Containers: original description and project price, empty weight and capacity; 2014 rules baseline. Liquid measure is the US pint.
source.license: Original project content; distribution license pending.

name: Waterskin
description:
A supple leather water carrier with sealed seams, a wooden stopper and a shoulder cord. It lies nearly flat when empty and is intended for drinking water carried on the road.

Holds up to 2 US quarts with a 4 lb contents limit. Sold empty. For this catalogue's game weights, a full load of water adds 4 lb, making the filled waterskin 4.5 lb. Emptying it removes the water's weight, not the skin's own weight.

weight.notes: Adjusted empty weight includes leather, stopper and cord. A full game-weight water load is 4 lb additional, for 4.5 lb total; water must be tracked separately.

source.title: Devil's Table: Goods & Provisions
source.reference: General Store / Containers: original description and project price, empty weight and capacity; 2014 rules baseline. Water uses a gameplay allowance of 2 lb per US quart.
source.license: Original project content; distribution license pending.

name: Clay Jug
description:
A plain earthenware jug with a broad belly, one handle and a glazed interior. Its pouring lip makes it useful for carrying water from a well or serving drinks at a table.

Holds up to 1 US gallon with an 8 lb contents limit. The open mouth has no stopper, so it must be kept upright during transport. Sold empty. It is breakable household pottery and is not intended for cooking over a fire.

weight.notes: Adjusted empty weight for a plain clay jug and handle; excludes liquids and any separately improvised cover.

source.title: Devil's Table: Goods & Provisions
source.reference: General Store / Containers: original description and project price, empty weight and capacity; 2014 rules baseline. Liquid measure is the US gallon.
source.license: Original project content; distribution license pending.

name: Ceramic Jar
description:
A wide-mouthed glazed jar with a fitted ceramic lid. It is convenient for salt, dried herbs, preserves or other small supplies that need a reusable covered vessel.

Holds up to 1 US quart with a 2 lb contents limit. The lid rests in place but does not make a watertight seal; wax or a separate binding is needed for secure travel. Sold empty with its lid. The ceramic can break if dropped.

weight.notes: Adjusted empty weight includes the glazed ceramic body and fitted lid; excludes sealing wax, bindings and contents.

source.title: Devil's Table: Goods & Provisions
source.reference: General Store / Containers: original description and project price, empty weight and capacity; 2014 rules baseline. Liquid measure is the US quart.
